descriptions: Before the patch, failure of devm_add_action_or_reset() consumed dbg with scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup as a registered reset action and then the error branch explicitly called scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg) again, allowing the same resources owned by dbg, including dbg->name according to the patch context, to be freed twice. After the patch, the failure path returns NULL immediately and relies only on devm_add_action_or_reset()'s reset action to perform cleanup once.

semantic_payload.label: Functions implicated by removed or fixed code

suggestions: First-draft detector should anchor on a call to devm_add_action_or_reset(dev, cleanup_fn, arg) used as an if-condition or error-check, where the failure branch directly calls cleanup_fn(arg).
The most precise patch-local sink is the deleted explicit call scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg), not the return NULL or formatting change.

Model devm_add_action_or_reset() as a barrier/reset API that invokes the supplied cleanup callback with the supplied argument on failure; then flag duplicate manual cleanup of the same callback and same argument on that failure path.
Use local AST plus local CFG within the affected function first; no cross-file analysis is needed for the initial checker because the callback and argument identity are visible at the call site.

Treat exact callback identity and exact argument identity as strong first-pass conditions; details of what scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup frees, such as dbg->name, can be a secondary refinement rather than a required initial match.
Do not require a separate free() call in the same function; the vulnerability is duplicated cleanup callback execution, where the actual free may be inside the callback.

patterns: Remove the explicit scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg) call from the devm_add_action_or_reset() failure branch.
Keep the early return NULL after devm_add_action_or_reset() failure so the setup function stops without a second cleanup invocation.
Rely on devm_add_action_or_reset() to run scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup on failure instead of manually duplicating the cleanup action.
